prTitle: feat(storage): use pagination for storage bucket list
stackAndServices: TypeScript/Next.js (Studio frontend: apps/studio, React Query, virtualized table) + Storage backend (supabase-js storage-js client calling the real storage-api service's GET /bucket endpoint) + Playwright e2e helpers. No storage-api backend source lives in this monorepo — the backend contract is external.
compiledPromise: Discriminating claim: 'When a project has more buckets than the page size, a user scrolling the Storage > Buckets list triggers server-driven pagination (offset-based, via supabase.storage.listBuckets({limit,offset,sortColumn,sortOrder,search})) that surfaces every bucket exactly once, in the selected sort order, across all loaded pages — including a bucket created by the user during the scroll session — with no duplicates and no drops, verified against a fresh-session reload of the same paginated view.' Negative: 'no bucket is rendered twice and no pre-existing bucket silently disappears from the aggregate paginated result set, even when a new bucket is created (an insert into storage.buckets) while the user is mid-scroll.' Companion quantifier-scoped claim: 'typing a search term shows only name-matching buckets across ALL loaded pages' requires >=2 matching bucket instantiations + >=1 non-matching negative per FW-11/1.4.
conjureFeasibility: Real, but expensive. CONJURE is mechanically possible entirely through the front door: create >100 buckets (DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE) via the Studio 'New bucket' dialog, then scroll. Nothing about the feature requires a stub or forces CND. The cost is scale, not mechanism: honoring the front-door-only constraint (no direct storage-api seeding) means ~100+ sequential UI actions just to reach page 2, which the calibrated mutation-attribution mechanism (1.2) must correctly treat as idle-baseline setup rather than claim-relevant window noise, even though every one of those writes lands in the exact claim-relevant table (storage.buckets). Confirmed independently via Supabase's self-hosting-storage API reference that the storage-api backend genuinely supports limit/offset/sortColumn/sortOrder/search on GET /bucket — this is NOT a client-only illusion; the params are real and honored server-side.
verdictBasis: The mechanism visible in the diff is fatal to the strict claim without needing execution: getNextPageParam uses pages.length as the next page NUMBER, and getBucketsPaginated converts that to offset = page * limit. This is offset-based (not cursor-based) pagination. Buckets are sorted by created_at desc by default. If a new bucket is created while the user has already loaded page 1 (offset 0-99) and then loads page 2 (offset 100-199), the newly created bucket shifts into position 0, pushing every other bucket down by one slot — the bucket that used to sit at the page-1/page-2 boundary (position 99) reappears at position 100 and gets rendered a second time on page 2. This is the standard, well-known failure mode of offset pagination combined with a mutable, recency-sorted list, and it is directly forced by the code's own page-number-based offset math, not a hypothetical. Confession: I could not execute the harness, so this is a structural prediction from the algorithm, not an observed run; the happy-path claim (scroll down, more buckets load, IO sentinel fires fetchNextPage) very plausibly WORKS in isolation. notCovered: sort-by-name path (alphabetical, not time-ordered) does not suffer the same insert-shift problem unless the new bucket's name sorts before the page boundary, so the failure is claim/sort-path-specific, not universal — a real harness run could stratify by sort mode and return a split verdict (WORKS for name-sort in most cases, DOES_NOT_WORK for created_at-sort) rather than one global answer.
holds: 1.1 write-set-bound oracle maps cleanly onto the compound claim once pagination correctness is tied to a bucket-creation write: the storage.buckets INSERT is a clean, harness-observable persisted-state delta, dual-leg-able (direct DB read as the persisted leg; a fresh Studio reload of the paginated list as the fresh-session leg).

1.2 mutation-attribution is unambiguous here: bucket creation via the UI is FK-causal to the acting project ref, and a pure list/scroll/search action should touch zero other tables — any unexplained write outside storage.buckets during the scroll window would be a legitimate fatal signal.

1.4 quantifier lint is directly load-bearing and earns its keep: the search claim ('only matching buckets show') and the aggregate-pagination claim ('every bucket appears exactly once') are both any/all-shaped and would collapse to an owner-shadow false-WORKS with a single seeded bucket; the theory correctly forces >=2 matching instantiations + a non-matching negative before either claim can be marked confirmed.
EGRESS (1.5) correctly does not apply — there is no outbound-call effect in this feature, and the theory does not force one artificially.

breaks.detail: The feature's advertised behavior (pagination, sort, search over already-persisted buckets) is a pure read/projection with no write of its own. Property P'(b) is built around a persisted-state delta; a naive application of the theory to a pure list/paginate/search/sort feature finds no delta to bind to and would default to NOT-EXECUTED -> CND on the very claims that matter most (correct paging math, dedup, ordering), even though the feature is fully exercisable. The only way to get a valid effect check is a deliberate reframing: manufacture a write (create one more bucket) and bind the read-correctness claim to that write's fresh-session visibility. This reframing is not automatic from the theory's text and is easy for an agent to miss, defaulting every list/search/sort/filter-shaped feature to a spurious CND instead of a real verdict.
breaks.fix: Add an explicit theory clause for read/projection-shaped claims: when the feature has no first-party write, the harness constructs a synthetic minimal write (one new entity via the front door) solely to create a fresh, harness-known delta, and binds the read/order/pagination claim to that delta's placement in the read surface — making this construction a required step, not an optional interpretive leap.

breaks.detail: Reaching page 2 requires seeding >DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE (100) buckets through the front door before the actual discriminating action can even be attempted. The theory's calibrated mutation-attribution treats pre-window writes as idle-baseline, but here 100+ setup writes land in the exact claim-relevant table (storage.buckets) that the effect check will later diff against. The theory doesn't specify how the harness cleanly separates a long multi-step setup phase (same table, same actor) from the single discriminating action's window without either miscounting setup writes as part of the tested delta, or requiring an artificial checkpoint/reset between setup and test that itself isn't 'user-shaped'.
breaks.fix: Define an explicit SETUP phase distinct from the ACTION WINDOW: writes during SETUP are baseline regardless of table, and the window opens only at the first action after setup completes; require the agent to declare the setup/window boundary in its pre-registered claim so the harness can enforce it mechanically.

breaks.detail: The load-more mechanism fires off a useIntersectionObserver callback triggered by real viewport scroll position, inside a virtualized table. The front-door constraint bars JS injection, but it's genuinely ambiguous whether a Playwright-style programmatic scroll (element.scrollBy / scrollIntoView) counts as a native user gesture or as injection that could force-trigger the IO callback without a believable scroll motion. Get this wrong in either direction: too strict and every virtualization/IO-driven feature becomes NOT-EXECUTED -> CND; too loose and an agent can manufacture an artificial WORKS by snapping to a scroll position no real trackpad/wheel input would produce.
breaks.fix: Add a driver-capability rule: scroll actions must be dispatched as native wheel/touch events (not element.scrollTo/scrollIntoView) so IO callbacks fire exactly as they would for a real user; classify any harness using DOM-method scrolling as a stub for that interaction class.

breaks.detail: Search has a 250ms debounce plus keepPreviousData:true on the infinite query. A hostile probe that reads results immediately after typing (before debounce fires) would see stale (previous, unfiltered) results, which is correct behavior but easy to misclassify as a failed filter if the agent doesn't know the 250ms constant. Extracting this timing constant from the diff and building a probe that respects it (or explicitly waits past it before asserting) requires close reading a lower-effort agent could skip, either producing a false failing hostile check or skipping the race check entirely.

sonnetDifficulty: Two things were genuinely hard for me as a Sonnet-level agent. First, the target repo (supabase/supabase) doesn't contain the storage-api backend source — the diff only shows the frontend calling supabase.storage.listBuckets({limit,offset,sortColumn,sortOrder,search}). Without cross-checking Supabase's own self-hosting-storage API docs via web search, I could not tell whether this was a real, backend-honored capability or a frontend-only illusion (params silently dropped server-side, which would make the whole feature fake and any 'page 2 differs from page 1' check a potential false-WORKS if the backend just returns the same top-N regardless of offset). That verification step is easy to skip under time pressure and isn't something the diff alone tells you. Second, recognizing that a pure read/pagination/search feature has no native write to bind an effect check to, and that the fix is to manufacture a synthetic write (create one bucket) and bind the read-correctness claim to it, took deliberate effort — the more obvious (and wrong) move is to shrug and call it NOT-EXECUTED/CND for lack of an obvious delta. Spotting the page-number-based offset math as a concrete insert-shift bug (rather than a vague 'pagination might have edge cases') required literally tracing getNextPageParam -> page*limit -> sort-by-created_at-desc by hand; a less careful pass would likely have stopped at 'looks fine, scroll loads more' and missed the concrete failure mode entirely.
newVectors: Read/projection-shaped features (pagination, sort, search, filter, any pure list view) have no first-party write to bind P'(b)'s effect check to; the theory needs an explicit synthetic-write construction rule or every such feature defaults to a spurious CND.

Multi-step setup-at-scale (seeding N>>1 entities through the front door before the real discriminating action is even possible) creates ambiguity between 'setup phase' and 'action window' when setup writes land in the exact claim-relevant table the effect check diffs against.

Driver authenticity boundary for observer/virtualization-triggered interactions (IntersectionObserver-driven infinite scroll): unclear whether programmatic scroll dispatch is a legitimate 'walk' primitive or an injection-adjacent shortcut, in either direction risking a false CND or a manufactured false WORKS.
openQuestions: Does the harness's driver have a native-scroll-gesture primitive, or would it fall back to DOM-method scrolling for virtualized lists — and does the theory currently classify that fallback as a stub?
How should the harness's setup/window boundary be declared and enforced when a feature requires bulk front-door seeding before the discriminating action is reachable?

Would a real execution confirm the offset-based page-shift duplication predicted from the code alone, or does keepPreviousData/React Query's cache dedupe by bucket id mask it at the render layer even though the raw paginated fetch would show the duplicate?
